findings.reason: The protected SQLite query applies julianday to both join columns, forcing a pairwise scan. The candidate transforms only the previous date and leaves current.recordDate available for an automatic equality index; on 8,192 daily rows it measured about 5 ms versus about 3.04 seconds for the protected query.

The branch previously claimed O(n log n), but the immutable MySQL DATEDIFF join and aligned SQLite two-sided date-function join have an O(n^2) worst case under the declared schema. The required bound now records that honest acceptance boundary; the staged candidate improves it to O(n log n).

The unchanged legal 8/64/256-row tiers are now bound explicitly to Weather row count and the quadratic immutable reference. A correct nested repeated-work control passed every output but failed scaling at +1.06 relative exponent and 47.97x on the largest tier; the candidate passed all three tiers.

The protected app-local and Accepted native sources remain untouched and retain their hash-bound SQLite-versus-MySQL date-arithmetic review. The candidate preserves exact calendar adjacency and strict temperature comparison but is inert and is not submission evidence.
